## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	上一讲（u1-l1）我们站在项目外面看清了 fast-ulysses 要解决的问题：把 Ulysses 序列并行的两次 4D all-to-all 从关键路径上挪开。本讲我们打开这个问题本身——**这两次 all-to-all 到底交换了什么、为什么恰好是两次、为什么中间夹的正好是注意力**。

26	| `n_global` | 注意力头总数；`n_local = head_splits[本rank]` 是本 rank 分到的头 |
27	| `s_global` | 全局序列长度；`s_local = seq_splits[本rank]` 是本 rank 分到的序列段 |

29

31	
32	### 2.2 集合通信与 all-to-all
33	
34	- **集合通信（collective）**：所有 rank 一起参与的通信原语，如 broadcast、all-gather、all-reduce。
35	- **all-to-all**：每个 rank 都给其他每个 rank（包括自己）发一块数据，同时从每个 rank 收一块数据。它是"交换分片方式"的最自然原语：发出去的是自己多出来的那份，收进来的是自己缺的那份。
36	
37	### 2.3 注意力按头独立
38	
39	缩放点积注意力对每个头 \( h \) 独立计算：
40	
41	\[
42	\mathrm{Attention}(Q_h, K_h, V_h) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{Q_h K_h^\top}{\sqrt{d}}\right) V_h
43	\]
44	
45	关键性质：**头与头之间没有任何数据交换**。softmax 混合的只是同一头内部的 token（序列轴）。整个 Ulysses 方案成立的根基就是这一条——把头切开分给不同 rank，注意力计算本身不需要任何额外通信。
46	
47	### 2.4 SPMD
48	
49	Single Program Multiple Data：每个 rank 运行**同一个程序**，各自处理自己那份数据。torchrun 启动的训练脚本就是这种形态。这意味着代码里没有 `if rank == 0: 做A; else: 做B` 式的分工——所有 rank 执行同一条语句序列，只是数据不同。这一点直接决定了 4.4 节的调用契约。

69	### 4.1 mode 0 / mode 1：一次交换的精确语义
70	
71	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
72	
73	长序列训练时，一张卡放不下整个序列的激活，于是把**序列切开**：rank r 拿到第 r 段（长度 `s_r = seq_splits[r]`），但拿**全部** `n_global` 个头。问题马上出现：注意力需要同一头看到**完整**序列才能算 `Q K^T`，而现在的每个 rank 只有片段。
74	
75	Ulysses 的解法是一次"交换商品"：**用我的序列分片换你的头分片**。交换之后，rank 持有完整序列但只有 `1/ws` 的头——由 2.3 节的性质，注意力照样能算，而且每 rank 的注意力计算量降到原来的 `1/ws`。算完再换回来。
76	
77	- **mode 0（scatter heads, gather sequence）**：序列分片 + 全部头 → 完整序列 + 头分片。注意力**之前**调用。
78	- **mode 1（gather heads, scatter sequence）**：mode 0 的严格逆变换。注意力**之后**调用。
79	
80	"scatter"指把本来聚在一起的轴（所有头）打散到各 rank，"gather"指把本来分散的轴（各 rank 的序列段）聚成完整序列。mode 0 同时做两件事：scatter 头、gather 序列。

96	\]
97	
98	**mode 1**：rank \( r \) 持有 \( y_r \in \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_{\text{global}} \times h_r \times d} \)，发给 peer \( p \) 的是一个**序列切片** \( y_r[:, S_p{:}S_{p+1}, :, :] \)，rank \( p \) 沿**头轴（dim 2）**拼接：

100	\[
101	z_p = \bigl\Vert_{r=0}^{ws-1} y_r[:, S_p{:}S_{p+1}, :, :] \bigr\vert_{\dim 2} \;\in\; \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_p \times n \times d}
102	\]
103	
104	**往返正确性**（为什么两次调用恰好复原，且是位精确的）：
105	
106	\( z_p \) 沿 dim 2 的第 \( r \) 段 = \( y_r \) 沿 dim 1 的第 \( p \) 段 = \( x_p[:, :, H_r{:}H_{r+1}, :] \)。于是
107	
108	\[
109	z_p = \bigl\Vert_{r} x_p[:, :, H_r{:}H_{r+1}, :] \bigr\vert_{\dim 2} = x_p[:, :, H_0{:}H_{ws}, :] = x_p
110	\]

246	### 4.2 包夹注意力：为什么两次通信中间正好放注意力
247	
248	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
249	
250	序列并行要解决的核心矛盾：**切序列**省下了显存与计算，但**注意力需要完整序列**。Ulysses 的回答是把通信放在注意力的两头，形成一个"三明治"：
251	
252	```
253	mode 0（交换） → 注意力（本地计算） → mode 1（交换回来）
254	```
255	
256	mode 0 之后每个 rank 持有 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`：**完整序列 × 我的头段**。由 2.3 节"头与头不通信"的性质，注意力在这一布局下完全本地——每个 rank 对自己的 `n_local` 个头、对着完整序列算 `softmax(QK^T)V`，期间零通信。mode 1 把布局换回"我的序列段 × 全部头"，让层的其余部分（LayerNorm、MLP 等逐 token 操作）继续按序列并行运转。
257	
258	反过来看这个三明治的**记账**：
259	
260	- 计算量：每 rank 注意力浮点量为 \( O(b \cdot n_{\text{local}} \cdot s_{\text{global}}^2 \cdot d) \)，是单卡全量 \( O(b \cdot n_{\text{global}} \cdot s_{\text{global}}^2 \cdot d) \) 的 \( 1/ws \)——序列并行让平方项的计算也被摊薄。
261	- 通信量：两次交换各搬全量张量的 \( 1/ws \)（见 4.1.2 的记账），与序列长度**线性**相关。
262	
263	于是有了对"关键路径"的定量直觉：注意力的计算量按 \( s^2 \) 增长但被摊到 `ws` 张卡上；通信按 \( s \) 线性增长且每层固定付两次、无法摊薄。序列越长，通信在每层耗时中的占比越高，最终成为瓶颈。用 README 快速开始的形状估算一笔账：`(1, 4096, 64, 128)` bf16 每个 rank 约 67 MB，每个注意力层两次交换 ≈ 每 rank 搬 134 MB；几十层的 DiT 一步就是每 rank 数 GB 的纯搬运。[README.md:11-13](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L11-L13) 说这两次集合通信是"the critical communication"，量级上就是这个意思；README 性能表（[README.md:34-39](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L34-L39)）里 base 路径在 H200 上花 1.569 ms、优化后仍要 0.860 ms 的，正是这两次交换。

368	**练习 2**：为什么例子在 mode 1 之前调用 `attn.contiguous()`（[examples/dit_attention.py:62](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py#L62)）？
369	
370	**答案**：SDPA 输出经过 `transpose(1, 2)` 后是非连续视图，而 `all_to_all_4d` 要求连续内存（库内部会 `.contiguous()`，见 [docs/api.md:49-50](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L49-L50)）。显式写出使数据流清晰，也避免依赖库的隐式整理。

372	**练习 3**：mode 0 之后每 rank 的显存里激活是变大了还是变小了？
373	
374	**答案**：形状从 `(b, s_local, n_global, 3d)` 变为 `(b, s_global, n_local, 3d)`，元素总数相同（偶均分时每 rank 元素数不变；不均匀时各 rank 略有差异）。所以三明治本身不省注意力输入的激活显存——它省的是**计算**（每头摊到 `ws` 份里）并保证通信量最小（每 rank 只搬 `1/ws` 全量）。省激活显存靠的是序列切分本身（每 rank 只需为 `s_local` 段保存层间激活）。

376	### 4.3 qkv 打包：一次握手搬完三份张量
377	
378	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
379	
380	注意力需要 q、k、v 三份张量，朴素做法是各做一次交换——**六次**集合调用（每份 mode 0 + mode 1）。但观察三份张量的形状：都是 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)`。把它们沿最后一维拼成 `(b, s_local, n_global, 3d)`，两次交换就能搬完全部字节。
381	
382	为什么"字节相同却更快"？因为一次集合调用的开销不只是带宽：库的每次调用都包含两道屏障内核与 copy-out（[docs/design.md:28-29](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L28-L29)），屏障是所有 rank 的会合点，吃的是**延迟**而非带宽。三次独立交换 = 每层 6 次调用；打包后 = 2 次调用。同样的字节，握手次数降到 1/3，且更大的单次消息对带宽利用更友好。quickstart 的原话（[docs/quickstart.md:27-28](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L27-L28)）："one call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three"。
383	
384	注意"打包进最后一维"这个位置选择的正确性：mode 0/1 只重排前三维（batch、序列、头），最后一维 `d` 整体随行移动——所以 `3d` 与 `d` 在交换语义下没有区别，`chunk(3, dim=-1)` 在交换前后都合法。
385	
386	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
387	
388	```
389	投影层输出 (b, s_local, n_global * 3d)
390	   └─ view → (b, s_local, n_global, 3d)     # 纯视图，零拷贝
391	        └─ all_to_all_4d(mode=0) → (b, s_global, n_local, 3d)
392	             └─ chunk(3, dim=-1) → q, k, v 各 (b, s_global, n_local, d)
393	                  └─ SDPA → (b, s_global, n_local, d)
394	                       └─ all_to_all_4d(mode=1) → (b, s_local, n_global, d)
395	```
396	
397	对比朴素方案：
398	
399	| 方案 | 每层集合调用数 | 每层搬运字节（每 rank） |
400	| --- | --- | --- |
401	| q、k、v 各自交换 | 6 | \( 6 \cdot b\, s_{\text{local}}\, n_{\text{global}}\, d\, e \) |
402	| 打包成 `3d` | 2 | \( 2 \cdot b\, s_{\text{local}}\, n_{\text{global}}\, (3d)\, e \)（相同） |

478	### 4.4 SPMD 调用契约：所有 rank 发出相同的形状序列
479	
480	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
481	
482	SPMD 意味着每个 rank 跑同一段程序。集合通信进一步要求：**会合点必须对齐**——每个 rank 到达某次集合调用时，其他 rank 也得到达同一次调用。对 fast-ulysses 来说，这条纪律具体化为"**每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状（和 dtype）序列**"。
483	
484	这条契约的来源在库的内部设计里：第一次遇到新形状的调用会分配一块对称内存窗口，而这个分配是集合操作——所有 rank 必须一起到齐才能完成（[docs/quickstart.md:92-94](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L92-L94)）。若某个 rank 走了别人没走的分支（比如 `if rank == 0` 里多发了一次调用），它会在集合点等永远不来的同伴——**挂起，不报错，不超时**（[docs/api.md:8](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L8) 原话："Violating these hangs the group. Nothing raises and nothing times out."）。
485	
486	好消息是：这**不是新纪律**。`torch.distributed` 的任何集合通信本来就要求同样的对齐，quickstart 特别指出"这是 `torch.distributed` 集合通信已经要求的同一种纪律"（[docs/quickstart.md:94](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L94)）。在 Ulysses 的典型用法里它自动满足：所有 rank 跑同一个模型同一层，自然发出相同的形状序列。
487	
488	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
489	
490	契约清单（摘自 [docs/api.md:6-20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L6-L20)，本讲关注第 1 条，其余在后续讲义展开）：
491	
492	1. **每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状序列**——新形状的首次调用触发集合的窗口分配。
493	2. 构造、`empty_output()`、`destroy()` 都是集合操作。
494	3. 每个 rank 必须发出相同的 **dtype 序列**（窗口按 `(role, dtype)` 分配，u4-l2）。
495	4. autograd 下，各 rank 的引擎必须以相同顺序到达 backward 节点（u6-l3）。
496	5. 一个缓冲同一时刻只服务一个调用（u4-l3）。
497	
498	```
499	健康路径：                             病理路径：
500	rank0: a2a(S1) a2a(S2) a2a(S1)         rank0: a2a(S1) a2a(S1) a2a(S2)
501	rank1: a2a(S1) a2a(S2) a2a(S1)         rank1: a2a(S1) ------  a2a(S2)
502	                                       rank1 的第 2 次调用等 rank0 的第 2 次调用
503	                                       ——双方在窗口分配处互相等待 → 挂起
504	```

575	**答案**：检测本身需要通信（rank 间对账），而对账又是一次需要全体参与的集合操作——用它来守护其他集合操作，鸡生蛋问题。挂起是集合通信的通用失败模式，`torch.distributed` 亦然，所以项目选择把它写成文档纪律（api.md 的 Collective contract 一节）而非运行时检查。理解这一点对阅读第 9 单元的对抗性测试（故意制造竞态与挂起）很重要。
576	
577	## 5. 综合实践
578	
579	**任务：在单进程里写一个"迷你 Ulysses"，把本讲四个模块串起来。**
580	
581	要求（示例代码骨架，CPU 可运行）：
582	
583	1. **基础件**（4.1）：实现 `scatter_head` / `gather_head`（4.1.4 已给出），断言 `gather_head(scatter_head(xs))` 位精确还原——这就是 mode 0/1 互逆。
584	2. **三明治**（4.2）：仿照 [examples/dit_attention.py:45-63](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py#L45-L63) 写 `ulysses_attention(x_list, ...)`：mode 0 → 每 rank 本地 SDPA → mode 1；用 4.2.4 的方法与"单进程全量"参照做 `allclose` 双校验（输出**和**输入梯度——给 `x_list` 设 `requires_grad`，两侧 `sum().backward()` 后比较梯度，完整镜像 [examples/dit_attention.py:96-116](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py#L96-L116) 的两条比较）。
585	3. **打包**（4.3）：输入用 `3 * head_dim` 最后一维的打包形式（q/k/v 在投影后 `view` 进来），确认集合调用次数是 2 而不是 6。
586	4. **契约反思**（4.4）：在代码注释里回答——你的单进程模拟里，"所有 rank 发出相同形状序列"这条契约对应什么？（答案：你给列表里每个元素发的调用序列完全相同；真实多进程下这点由 SPMD 程序结构保证，而任何 `if rank == ...` 的条件调用都会破坏它。）
587	
588	**验收标准**：往返位精确 `True`；三明治输出与梯度 `allclose` 通过（float32/CPU 建议先试 `atol=1e-5`）；调用计数 2。全部**待本地验证**。通过后，建议在装好库的环境里跑一次真实版：`torchrun --nproc_per_node=<N> examples/dit_attention.py`，把它打印的 `output max |diff|` / `d/dinput max |diff|` 与你单进程模拟的误差量级对照（bf16 下容差是 `5e-2`，见 [examples/dit_attention.py:113](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py#L113)）。
589	
590	## 6. 本讲小结
591	
592	- **mode 0 / mode 1 是一对互逆的形状变换**：mode 0 把 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` 换成 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`——每个 rank 发出头切片、沿序列轴收回；mode 1 反向。往返是纯搬运，位精确。
593	- **三明治结构**：mode 0 → 注意力 → mode 1。注意力按头独立的性质让"完整序列 × 头分片"布局下的计算完全本地，计算量摊薄 `ws` 倍，通信量每 rank 只有全量的 `1/ws`。
594	- **长序列下通信是关键路径**：通信字节随 `s` 线性增长且每层固定付两次，不被 `ws` 摊薄；这是整个项目存在的理由。
595	- **qkv 打包**：三份 `(b, s, n, d)` 拼成 `(b, s, n, 3d)`，字节不变、握手次数从每层 6 次降到 2 次（屏障从 12 道降到 4 道）。
596	- **SPMD 契约**：每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状/dtype 序列，根源是新形状首次调用触发的窗口分配是集合操作；违反的后果是挂起而非报错——这与 `torch.distributed` 的既有纪律同源。
597

# 讲义 u1-l2：Ulysses 序列并行原理：两次 all-to-all 包夹注意力

## 1. 本讲目标

上一讲（u1-l1）我们站在项目外面看清了 fast-ulysses 要解决的问题：把 Ulysses 序列并行的两次 4D all-to-all 从关键路径上挪开。本讲我们打开这个问题本身——**这两次 all-to-all 到底交换了什么、为什么恰好是两次、为什么中间夹的正好是注意力**。

学完本讲你应当能：

1. 画出 mode 0 / mode 1 前后的张量形状：mode 0 把每个 rank 的 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` 变成 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`，mode 1 是它的逆。
2. 解释为什么长序列 DiT 训练里这两个集合通信成为关键路径（字节量随序列长度线性增长，且每层都要付两次）。
3. 理解 q/k/v 打包进最后一维（`3 * head_dim`）为什么能在字节量不变的前提下，把三次握手压成一次。
4. 说出 SPMD 调用契约：每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状序列，违反的后果是**挂起**而不是报错。

本讲全程不需要 GPU：所有实践都可以在单进程、纯 CPU 的 torch 上完成——这与项目自己的哲学一致（布局语义可以在主机上验证，见 [docs/design.md:37-39](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L37-L39)）。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 形状记号

全手册统一使用（与 [docs/api.md:3-4](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L3-L4) 一致）：

| 记号 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| `b` | batch 大小 |
| `d` | 每个注意力头的维度（head dim） |
| `n_global` | 注意力头总数；`n_local = head_splits[本rank]` 是本 rank 分到的头 |
| `s_global` | 全局序列长度；`s_local = seq_splits[本rank]` 是本 rank 分到的序列段 |
| `ws` | world size，即 rank 数 |

4D 张量 `(b, s, n, d)` 的轴含义是：batch、序列（token）、注意力头、头的通道。

### 2.2 集合通信与 all-to-all

- **集合通信（collective）**：所有 rank 一起参与的通信原语，如 broadcast、all-gather、all-reduce。
- **all-to-all**：每个 rank 都给其他每个 rank（包括自己）发一块数据，同时从每个 rank 收一块数据。它是"交换分片方式"的最自然原语：发出去的是自己多出来的那份，收进来的是自己缺的那份。

### 2.3 注意力按头独立

缩放点积注意力对每个头 \( h \) 独立计算：

\[
\mathrm{Attention}(Q_h, K_h, V_h) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{Q_h K_h^\top}{\sqrt{d}}\right) V_h
\]

关键性质：**头与头之间没有任何数据交换**。softmax 混合的只是同一头内部的 token（序列轴）。整个 Ulysses 方案成立的根基就是这一条——把头切开分给不同 rank，注意力计算本身不需要任何额外通信。

### 2.4 SPMD

Single Program Multiple Data：每个 rank 运行**同一个程序**，各自处理自己那份数据。torchrun 启动的训练脚本就是这种形态。这意味着代码里没有 `if rank == 0: 做A; else: 做B` 式的分工——所有 rank 执行同一条语句序列，只是数据不同。这一点直接决定了 4.4 节的调用契约。

### 2.5 承接上一讲

u1-l1 已点名的术语——拷贝引擎（CE）、对称内存、mode 0/1——本讲给出精确定义；CE 传输如何兑现这些形状变换则留给第 5 单元（u5-l1）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 本讲用它做什么 |
| --- | --- |
| [README.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L11-L13) | 项目对 Ulysses 的一段官方定义；快速开始里的形状示例 |
| [docs/quickstart.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L3-L5) | "两次调用包夹注意力"的最小代码；qkv 打包建议；"什么会让你挂起" |
| [examples/dit_attention.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/examples/dit_attention.py#L1-L17) | 一个真实的序列并行注意力块：两次调用、qkv 打包、双路校验 |
| [test/test_plan.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/test_plan.py#L72-L87) | mode 0/1 语义的**纯 numpy 参照实现**——本讲实践的对照答案 |
| [include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp#L12-L17) | mode 0/1 的 C++ 枚举定义，形状注释是全项目最浓缩的语义说明 |
| [python/fast_ulysses/group.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L111-L128) | Python 侧 `all_to_all_4d` 签名与 docstring 中的契约陈述 |
| [docs/api.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L42-L47) | mode 与输入输出形状的官方对照表；集合契约清单 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 mode 0 / mode 1：一次交换的精确语义

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

长序列训练时，一张卡放不下整个序列的激活，于是把**序列切开**：rank r 拿到第 r 段（长度 `s_r = seq_splits[r]`），但拿**全部** `n_global` 个头。问题马上出现：注意力需要同一头看到**完整**序列才能算 `Q K^T`，而现在的每个 rank 只有片段。

Ulysses 的解法是一次"交换商品"：**用我的序列分片换你的头分片**。交换之后，rank 持有完整序列但只有 `1/ws` 的头——由 2.3 节的性质，注意力照样能算，而且每 rank 的注意力计算量降到原来的 `1/ws`。算完再换回来。

- **mode 0（scatter heads, gather sequence）**：序列分片 + 全部头 → 完整序列 + 头分片。注意力**之前**调用。
- **mode 1（gather heads, scatter sequence）**：mode 0 的严格逆变换。注意力**之后**调用。

"scatter"指把本来聚在一起的轴（所有头）打散到各 rank，"gather"指把本来分散的轴（各 rank 的序列段）聚成完整序列。mode 0 同时做两件事：scatter 头、gather 序列。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

设头偏移 \( H_p = \sum_{j<p} h_j \)，序列偏移 \( S_p = \sum_{j<p} s_j \)（\( h_j, s_j \) 分别是 `head_splits[j]`、`seq_splits[j]`；\( H_0 = S_0 = 0 \)）。

**mode 0**：rank \( r \) 持有 \( x_r \in \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_r \times n \times d} \)（\( n = n_{\text{global}} \)）。它发给 peer \( p \) 的是自己张量的一个**头切片**：

\[
x_r[:,\; :,\; H_p{:}H_{p+1},\; :] \;\in\; \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_r \times h_p \times d}
\]

rank \( p \) 把来自所有 rank 的块**沿序列轴（dim 1）按 rank 序**拼接，得到输出：

\[
y_p = \bigl\Vert_{r=0}^{ws-1} x_r[:, :, H_p{:}H_{p+1}, :] \bigr\vert_{\dim 1} \;\in\; \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_{\text{global}} \times h_p \times d}
\]

**mode 1**：rank \( r \) 持有 \( y_r \in \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_{\text{global}} \times h_r \times d} \)，发给 peer \( p \) 的是一个**序列切片** \( y_r[:, S_p{:}S_{p+1}, :, :] \)，rank \( p \) 沿**头轴（dim 2）**拼接：

\[
z_p = \bigl\Vert_{r=0}^{ws-1} y_r[:, S_p{:}S_{p+1}, :, :] \bigr\vert_{\dim 2} \;\in\; \mathbb{R}^{b \times s_p \times n \times d}
\]

**往返正确性**（为什么两次调用恰好复原，且是位精确的）：

\( z_p \) 沿 dim 2 的第 \( r \) 段 = \( y_r \) 沿 dim 1 的第 \( p \) 段 = \( x_p[:, :, H_r{:}H_{r+1}, :] \)。于是

\[
z_p = \bigl\Vert_{r} x_p[:, :, H_r{:}H_{r+1}, :] \bigr\vert_{\dim 2} = x_p[:, :, H_0{:}H_{ws}, :] = x_p
\]

整个过程中只有切片和搬运，没有任何算术，所以往返是**位精确**（bit-exact）的——这是 [test/test_plan.py:236-237](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/test_plan.py#L236-L237) 敢用 `assert_array_equal` 的原因。

**通信量记账**（偶均分时）：mode 0 中每个 rank 发出 \( b \cdot s_{\text{local}} \cdot n_{\text{global}} \cdot d \) 个元素，收到 \( b \cdot s_{\text{global}} \cdot n_{\text{local}} \cdot d \) 个元素；由于 \( s_{\text{global}} = ws \cdot s_{\text{local}} \)、\( n_{\text{local}} = n_{\text{global}} / ws \)，两者相等——发多少收多少，正好是全量张量的 \( 1/ws \)。

**不均匀分片是一般路径**：上面的公式从未要求 \( s_r \) 或 \( h_p \) 相等。偶均分只是 \( s_j = s/P,\ h_j = n/P \) 的特例（[include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp:5-6](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp#L5-L6) 的注释原话）。允许某个 \( s_p = 0 \) 也是合法的（空序列段不发拷贝，见 [test/test_plan.py:179-181](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/test_plan.py#L179-L181)）。丢掉 padding 的收益在 u2-l3 展开。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① mode 的权威定义——C++ 枚举。** 全项目对 mode 0/1 最浓缩的语义说明只有两行注释：

[include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp:12-17](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/a2a_plan.hpp#L12-L17)

```cpp
enum A2AMode : int {
    // [b, seq_splits[me], head_total, d] -> [b, seq_total, head_splits[me], d]
    kScatterHead = 0,
    // the inverse: [b, seq_total, head_splits[me], d] -> [b, seq_splits[me], head_total, d]
    kGatherHead = 1,
};
```

这两行注释就是 mode 的完整契约：`kScatterHead = 0` 把"我的序列段 × 全部头"变成"全部序列 × 我的头段"，`kGatherHead = 1` 是逆变换。Python 侧的 `mode=0` / `mode=1` 直接映射到这个枚举。

**② 官方形状对照表。**

[docs/api.md:44-47](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L44-L47)

| mode | input | output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — scatter heads, gather sequence | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` |
| 1 — the inverse | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` |

**③ README 快速开始中的具体数字。**

[README.md:63-68](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L63-L68)

```python
b, s_local, heads, d = 1, 4096, 8, 128
ws = dist.get_world_size()
x = torch.randn(b, s_local, heads * ws, d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

y = group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)        # (b, s_local * ws, heads, d)
z = group.all_to_all_4d(y, mode=1)        # back to x's shape
```

注意这里的 `heads=8` 是**每 rank** 的头数（即 `n_local`），所以输入的头轴是 `heads * ws = 64 = n_global`。以 `ws=8` 代入：`x` 是 `(1, 4096, 64, 128)`，mode 0 之后 `y` 是 `(1, 32768, 8, 128)`——序列轴变长 8 倍，头轴缩短 8 倍，元素总数不变。mode 1 再换回 `(1, 4096, 64, 128)`。

**④ 语义的测试参照实现——本讲实践的"标准答案"。**

[test/test_plan.py:72-87](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/test_plan.py#L72-L87)

```python
def reference_scatter_head(inputs, head_splits):
    """[b, s_r, n_total, d] per rank -> [b, s_total, n_p, d] per rank.
    Rank p's output stacks, over source ranks r in order, the head columns
    p owns from rank r's local sequence shard."""
    head_off = np.cumsum([0] + list(head_splits))
    return [
        np.concatenate([x[:, :, head_off[p] : head_off[p + 1], :] for x in inputs], axis=1)
        for p in range(len(inputs))
    ]
```

### 4.2 包夹注意力：为什么两次通信中间正好放注意力

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

序列并行要解决的核心矛盾：**切序列**省下了显存与计算，但**注意力需要完整序列**。Ulysses 的回答是把通信放在注意力的两头，形成一个"三明治"：

```
mode 0（交换） → 注意力（本地计算） → mode 1（交换回来）
```

mode 0 之后每个 rank 持有 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`：**完整序列 × 我的头段**。由 2.3 节"头与头不通信"的性质，注意力在这一布局下完全本地——每个 rank 对自己的 `n_local` 个头、对着完整序列算 `softmax(QK^T)V`，期间零通信。mode 1 把布局换回"我的序列段 × 全部头"，让层的其余部分（LayerNorm、MLP 等逐 token 操作）继续按序列并行运转。

反过来看这个三明治的**记账**：

- 计算量：每 rank 注意力浮点量为 \( O(b \cdot n_{\text{local}} \cdot s_{\text{global}}^2 \cdot d) \)，是单卡全量 \( O(b \cdot n_{\text{global}} \cdot s_{\text{global}}^2 \cdot d) \) 的 \( 1/ws \)——序列并行让平方项的计算也被摊薄。
- 通信量：两次交换各搬全量张量的 \( 1/ws \)（见 4.1.2 的记账），与序列长度**线性**相关。

于是有了对"关键路径"的定量直觉：注意力的计算量按 \( s^2 \) 增长但被摊到 `ws` 张卡上；通信按 \( s \) 线性增长且每层固定付两次、无法摊薄。序列越长，通信在每层耗时中的占比越高，最终成为瓶颈。用 README 快速开始的形状估算一笔账：`(1, 4096, 64, 128)` bf16 每个 rank 约 67 MB，每个注意力层两次交换 ≈ 每 rank 搬 134 MB；几十层的 DiT 一步就是每 rank 数 GB 的纯搬运。[README.md:11-13](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L11-L13) 说这两次集合通信是"the critical communication"，量级上就是这个意思；README 性能表（[README.md:34-39](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L34-L39)）里 base 路径在 H200 上花 1.569 ms、优化后仍要 0.860 ms 的，正是这两次交换。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一个序列并行的 DiT 注意力块，前向伪代码：

```
输入 x: (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)          # 我持有的序列段，全部头
1. qkv = 投影(x) → view 成 (b, s_local, n_global, 3*head_dim)   # 4.3 节的打包
2. qkv = all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)               # → (b, s_global, n_local, 3*head_dim)
3. q, k, v = chunk(qkv, 3, dim=-1)
   attn = SDPA(q, k, v)                            # 完整序列 × 我的头段，零通信
   # → (b, s_global, n_local, head_dim)
4. out = all_to_all_4d(attn, mode=1)               # → (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
5. 返回 投影(out)
```

反向传播时两个mode自动互换角色：mode 0 的 vjp 是 mode 1、mode 1 的 vjp 是 mode 0（排列的 vjp 是逆排列），细节在 u6-l3。

def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    b, s_local, _ = x.shape
    qkv = self.qkv(x).view(b, s_local, self.n_global, 3 * self.head_dim)
    qkv = self.group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)  # (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
    q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    attn = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
    ).transpose(1, 2)  # (b, s_global, n_local, head_dim)
    attn = self.group.all_to_all_4d(attn.contiguous(), mode=1)
    return self.proj(attn.reshape(b, s_local, self.n_global * self.head_dim))

import torch.nn.functional as F

def ulysses_sandwich(x_list, seq_splits, head_splits):
    """x_list[r]: (b, s_r, n_global, 3*head_dim)。中间夹一个本地注意力。"""
    y_list = scatter_head(x_list, head_splits)          # mode 0
    out = []
    for y in y_list:                                     # 每"rank"：完整序列 × 自己的头段
        q, k, v = y.chunk(3, dim=-1)
        a = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
        ).transpose(1, 2)                                # (b, s_global, n_local, head_dim)
        out.append(a.contiguous())
    return gather_head(out, seq_splits)                  # mode 1

torch.manual_seed(1)
b, d, ws = 1, 16, 4
seq_splits, head_splits = [5, 5, 5, 5], [2, 2, 2, 2]
n_global = sum(head_splits)

full = torch.randn(b, sum(seq_splits), n_global, 3 * d)
x_list = [full[:, sum(seq_splits[:r]):sum(seq_splits[:r+1])] for r in range(ws)]

local_out = ulysses_sandwich(x_list, seq_splits, head_splits)
sandwiched = torch.cat(local_out, dim=1)                # 按 rank 序拼回全局

q, k, v = full.chunk(3, dim=-1)                         # 参照：不切分，直接算
ref = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
    q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
).transpose(1, 2)

print(torch.allclose(sandwiched, ref, atol=1e-5))

### 4.3 qkv 打包：一次握手搬完三份张量

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

注意力需要 q、k、v 三份张量，朴素做法是各做一次交换——**六次**集合调用（每份 mode 0 + mode 1）。但观察三份张量的形状：都是 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)`。把它们沿最后一维拼成 `(b, s_local, n_global, 3d)`，两次交换就能搬完全部字节。

为什么"字节相同却更快"？因为一次集合调用的开销不只是带宽：库的每次调用都包含两道屏障内核与 copy-out（[docs/design.md:28-29](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/design.md#L28-L29)），屏障是所有 rank 的会合点，吃的是**延迟**而非带宽。三次独立交换 = 每层 6 次调用；打包后 = 2 次调用。同样的字节，握手次数降到 1/3，且更大的单次消息对带宽利用更友好。quickstart 的原话（[docs/quickstart.md:27-28](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L27-L28)）："one call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three"。

注意"打包进最后一维"这个位置选择的正确性：mode 0/1 只重排前三维（batch、序列、头），最后一维 `d` 整体随行移动——所以 `3d` 与 `d` 在交换语义下没有区别，`chunk(3, dim=-1)` 在交换前后都合法。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
投影层输出 (b, s_local, n_global * 3d)
   └─ view → (b, s_local, n_global, 3d)     # 纯视图，零拷贝
        └─ all_to_all_4d(mode=0) → (b, s_global, n_local, 3d)
             └─ chunk(3, dim=-1) → q, k, v 各 (b, s_global, n_local, d)
                  └─ SDPA → (b, s_global, n_local, d)
                       └─ all_to_all_4d(mode=1) → (b, s_local, n_global, d)
```

对比朴素方案：

| 方案 | 每层集合调用数 | 每层搬运字节（每 rank） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| q、k、v 各自交换 | 6 | \( 6 \cdot b\, s_{\text{local}}\, n_{\text{global}}\, d\, e \) |
| 打包成 `3d` | 2 | \( 2 \cdot b\, s_{\text{local}}\, n_{\text{global}}\, (3d)\, e \)（相同） |

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么把 q/k/v 拼在**最后一维**，而不是拼在序列维或头维？

**答案**：mode 0/1 的重排只作用于 batch、序列、头三维，最后一维 `d` 是每行整体搬运的最小单元（库的对齐检查也是按 `d * elem_size` 计，见 [README.md:107-108](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/README.md#L107-L108)）。拼在最后一维，交换前后都能用零拷贝视图（`view` / `chunk`）打包拆包；拼在序列维或头维则会改变那些轴的分片含义，破坏 mode 的形状契约。

**练习 2**：三次独立交换与一次打包交换，带宽层面的字节数相同，那打包省下的开销具体是什么？

**答案**：省的是每调用的固定成本——两道屏障（全体 rank 的会合延迟）、调用的校验与发射开销；同时单条消息变大 3 倍，对带宽的利用率更好（大消息更容易打满链路，这也是本项目"面向每 rank 数百 MB 大消息"定位的一部分，见 u1-l1）。

**练习 3**：注意力输出 `attn` 是 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`，为什么 mode 1 之前不把它和别的张量打包？

**答案**：可以打包的对象得是"同一时刻、同方向、同形状"的交换。输出侧只有注意力结果一份（q/k/v 已在输入侧消费掉），没有可拼的同伴；而且 mode 1 之后它要进输出投影，拼了还得拆。打包的收益出现在"多份张量共享同一次交换"的场合——这里是输入侧的 q/k/v。

### 4.4 SPMD 调用契约：所有 rank 发出相同的形状序列

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

SPMD 意味着每个 rank 跑同一段程序。集合通信进一步要求：**会合点必须对齐**——每个 rank 到达某次集合调用时，其他 rank 也得到达同一次调用。对 fast-ulysses 来说，这条纪律具体化为"**每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状（和 dtype）序列**"。

这条契约的来源在库的内部设计里：第一次遇到新形状的调用会分配一块对称内存窗口，而这个分配是集合操作——所有 rank 必须一起到齐才能完成（[docs/quickstart.md:92-94](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L92-L94)）。若某个 rank 走了别人没走的分支（比如 `if rank == 0` 里多发了一次调用），它会在集合点等永远不来的同伴——**挂起，不报错，不超时**（[docs/api.md:8](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L8) 原话："Violating these hangs the group. Nothing raises and nothing times out."）。

好消息是：这**不是新纪律**。`torch.distributed` 的任何集合通信本来就要求同样的对齐，quickstart 特别指出"这是 `torch.distributed` 集合通信已经要求的同一种纪律"（[docs/quickstart.md:94](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/quickstart.md#L94)）。在 Ulysses 的典型用法里它自动满足：所有 rank 跑同一个模型同一层，自然发出相同的形状序列。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

契约清单（摘自 [docs/api.md:6-20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L6-L20)，本讲关注第 1 条，其余在后续讲义展开）：

1. **每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状序列**——新形状的首次调用触发集合的窗口分配。
2. 构造、`empty_output()`、`destroy()` 都是集合操作。
3. 每个 rank 必须发出相同的 **dtype 序列**（窗口按 `(role, dtype)` 分配，u4-l2）。
4. autograd 下，各 rank 的引擎必须以相同顺序到达 backward 节点（u6-l3）。
5. 一个缓冲同一时刻只服务一个调用（u4-l3）。

```
健康路径：                             病理路径：
rank0: a2a(S1) a2a(S2) a2a(S1)         rank0: a2a(S1) a2a(S1) a2a(S2)
rank1: a2a(S1) a2a(S2) a2a(S1)         rank1: a2a(S1) ------  a2a(S2)
                                       rank1 的第 2 次调用等 rank0 的第 2 次调用
                                       ——双方在窗口分配处互相等待 → 挂起
```

## 6. 本讲小结

- **mode 0 / mode 1 是一对互逆的形状变换**：mode 0 把 `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` 换成 `(b, s_global, n_local, d)`——每个 rank 发出头切片、沿序列轴收回；mode 1 反向。往返是纯搬运，位精确。
- **三明治结构**：mode 0 → 注意力 → mode 1。注意力按头独立的性质让"完整序列 × 头分片"布局下的计算完全本地，计算量摊薄 `ws` 倍，通信量每 rank 只有全量的 `1/ws`。
- **长序列下通信是关键路径**：通信字节随 `s` 线性增长且每层固定付两次，不被 `ws` 摊薄；这是整个项目存在的理由。
- **qkv 打包**：三份 `(b, s, n, d)` 拼成 `(b, s, n, 3d)`，字节不变、握手次数从每层 6 次降到 2 次（屏障从 12 道降到 4 道）。
- **SPMD 契约**：每个 rank 必须发出相同的形状/dtype 序列，根源是新形状首次调用触发的窗口分配是集合操作；违反的后果是挂起而非报错——这与 `torch.distributed` 的既有纪律同源。

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
